key_insight: OmniVBench introduces a large-scale benchmark and dataset designed for the next generation of reference-to-video generation, where models must handle many reference types and combinations. It shifts evaluation beyond simple overall similarity to check whether each reference factor is correctly preserved, separated, and assigned.
problem_solved: Existing R2V benchmarks do not cover the full range of emerging omni-reference scenarios, and their evaluation methods mostly judge holistic consistency instead of fine-grained control. This makes it hard to measure whether models truly use multiple references correctly, especially when reference information must be disentangled and routed.
method: Builds a benchmark with broader coverage of reference types and reference compositions for omni R2V generation.
Provides a large-scale dataset to support more realistic and diverse evaluation scenarios.
Introduces evaluation protocols that assess fine-grained preservation, disentanglement, and routing of reference factors rather than only overall output quality.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, OmniVBench offers a more realistic way to test and compare video generation models under complex reference-control settings. It can help identify failure modes that traditional benchmarks miss and guide development of more controllable, reliable R2V systems.

paper_title: OmniVBench: A Benchmark and Large-Scale Dataset for Omni Reference-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Wenxue Li, Peiyan Guan, Haoyang Jiang, Junxian Cai, Hualuo Liu
